reasoning_traces.think:
The kinetic translation deficit (KTD) models discrepancy between observed and predicted player velocities, serving as a proxy for tracking accuracy. It enables GSI to compute posterior belief updates in Bayesian motion forecasting. The reliability-attenuated transfer bounds (RATB) scale expected velocity changes according to sensor reliability, preventing overconfidence in stale data. These bounds are essential for GSE's state transition modeling, ensuring plausible player movement dynamics. The Drive+ Combine Grade aggregates three key metrics—drive velocity, tau resolution, and t5 response—into a single scalar for player evaluation. This grade acts as a dualistic input to both GSI’s probabilistic inference and GSE’s tactical decision-making engines. All three primitives exhibit dual behavior: KTD and RATB provide uncertainty quantification, while Drive+ offers structured aggregation. Failure modes include aliasing in KTD due to low sampling rates, loss of information in RATB when reliability drops, and degradation in Drive+ when individual components fail. These primitives collectively support a robust, mathematically grounded framework for integrating real-time tracking into predictive analytics and agent-based simulations.
